claims.claim_text: Arqit names 'government and defense customers' as the initial enterprise-license target market for its QuantumCloud symmetric-key product.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.source_quote: After initially focusing on selling enterprise licenses, especially to government and defense customers, Arqit made faster than expected progress in generating interest from large, global technology vendors, and has therefore switched its focus to securing distribution through channel partners.

claims.claim_text: Arqit lists the UK Government as a current customer of QuantumCloud.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.source_quote: Arqit's current customers include the UK Government, the European Space Agency, BT plc, Sumitomo Corporation, Virgin Orbit, AUCloud and Nine23.

claims.claim_text: Arqit names the European Space Agency (ESA) as a customer under the ARTES 33-11 programme line, with milestone-based payments for the QKDSat program.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.source_quote: QKDSat is constituted under the ARTES 33-11 programme line which ESA has created with the objective of validating Quantum Key Distribution technologies. ... Arqit is providing services to ESA in its capacity as a customer.

claims.claim_text: Arqit has signed channel partnerships with Fortinet, AWS, Dell, and TraxPay through which it expects to sell directly and indirectly to end customers (including downstream defense / government end users).
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.source_quote: Arqit recently announced important channel partnerships, including Fortinet, AWS, Dell, and TraxPay, through which it will sell directly and indirectly to end customers.

claims.claim_text: Arqit's symmetric-key product was independently reviewed and assured in May 2022 by the University of Surrey (a UK NCSC-accredited Centre of Excellence for Cyber Security), establishing UK-government-adjacent technical validation.
claims.subject: Arqit QuantumCloud
claims.object_value: University of Surrey (NCSC Centre of Excellence), May 2022
claims.source_quote: The security of the symmetric key agreement software created by Arqit was independently reviewed and assured in May 2022 by the University of Surrey, which is accredited as a Centre of Excellence for Cyber Security by the UK Government's National Cyber Security Centre.

claims.claim_text: Arqit subcontracts QKD satellite delivery to Qinetiq Space NV under a firm fixed-price contract signed January 27, 2020 with delivery expected May 2022 and a launch-readiness review by July 2022.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.object_value: Qinetiq Space NV (firm fixed-price; QKD satellite delivery May 2022)
claims.source_quote: On January 27, 2020, Arqit entered into a firm fixed price contract with Qinetiq Space NV or Qinetiq for delivery by Qinetiq of quantum key distribution satellites by May 2022 and for conducting a launch readiness review by July 2022.

claims.claim_text: Arqit pivoted away from the satellite-delivery component of its tech stack during 2022, removing satellites from QuantumCloud and shifting to a terrestrial classical-hardware method of replicated-entropy distribution.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.source_quote: It has removed, through innovation, the costly and complex satellite component from the tech stack of QuantumCloud, its software platform as a service.

claims.claim_text: Arqit booked a net profit of $65.575 million for FY ended September 30, 2022 — a result that the filing flags as driven by adjustments for non-cash items of $93.187 million (warrant fair-value movement), not operating cash generation.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.object_value: $65.575M (vs. $26.916M cash used in operations; +$93.187M non-cash adjustments)
claims.source_quote: During the year ended September 30, 2022 cash used in operating activities was $26.916 million. The primary factors affecting operating cash flows during the period were a net profit of $65.575 million and adjustments for non-cash items of $93.187 million.

claims.claim_text: Arqit's TAM is asserted as the entire global information-security market ($261.7B by end-2026 per Gartner), with government and IoT named as 'two of its key markets in the future' but explicitly excluded from the TAM estimate due to lack of reliable data.
claims.subject: Arqit
claims.object_value: $261.7B global infosec by 2026 (gov/IoT excluded from estimate)
claims.source_quote: According to Gartner, it is estimated that the global addressable market for information security services will be $261.7 billion by the end of 2026. ... Arqit's estimates of its total addressable market are limited by a lack of reliable data on the government and Internet of Things markets, which are therefore excluded from its total addressable market estimate, but which Arqit expects to be two of its key markets in the future.

extractor_notes: ARQQ 20-F (FY22, filed 2022-12-14) is notably LIGHT on specific Pentagon Program Elements. It names ZERO PE numbers (no 06xxxxxx, no SF/AF prefixes), ZERO named US DoD programs (no AFRL Quantum Networking, no DARPA / SDA / Skyborg references), ZERO 'X% of FY revenue from program Y' attributions, and ZERO claims of being a prime / sub on a named US DoD line. Defense exposure is asserted only at the highest level of generality ('government and defense customers'). The single named government customer is the UK Government (out-of-corpus for pentagon_jbook). The most specific 'program-of-record-like' claim is ESA's ARTES 33-11 line under QKDSat — also out of US Pentagon J-Book corpus. The pivot away from satellites (claim C7) implicitly orphans the original UK / ESA defense narrative tied to QKDSat. Cohort framing here: this is a NULL test case for the J-Book divergence pattern at this cutoff. The filing simply does not name US Pentagon programs to falsify.
